## TL;DR

Single-factor-at-a-time LoRA SFT sweep on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct testing whether #383's per-factor selectivity pattern (every recipe knob that lifts source-persona implantation also lifts source-vs-bystander selectivity) generalizes from a literal `[ZLT]` marker to **behavioral (sycophancy) implantation** on the same 3 source personas (librarian, programmer, surgeon).

- **15 LoRA cells:** anchor `10011` + 3 one-bit flips (A short-system `00011`, C neutral-framing `10111`, D base-Qwen-data `10001`) × 3 sources × seed 42 + 3 sanity-null `assistant_*` controls + 1 base-model zero-shot baseline.
- **Eval:** external `run_sycophancy_eval.py` AS-IS with a ~50 LOC persona-injection fork, run over 24 panel personas × 8 OUT configs (4 held-out of 11 scenarios × 2 perspectives) × 20 rollouts × 6 turns × logit A/B probe per turn.
- **Primary metric:** per-factor selectivity Δ on `mean_sycophancy_index` = mean-of-3-source-level-Δs (cluster mean); 23-bystander mean as headline + 23-bystander median as unconditional sensitivity column.
- **Hypothesis:** ≥2 of 3 swept factors show selectivity Δ CI clearing zero, same sign as #383. Median guess: 3 of 3.
- **Kill criterion:** all 3 swept factors have selectivity Δ CIs that include zero, OR best-cell source lift < +0.05.
- **3 forced design changes vs #383:** drop B-axis (eval owns conversational length), drop E-axis (no honest behavioral analog to marker-only loss), train/eval scenario split (sycophancy has memorization risk that markers don't).
